title: Ethiopian Urges BRICS Member States to Invest in Youth Led Digital, Green Growth
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has called on BRICS member states to establish dedicated funding mechanisms for youth enterprises and increase investment in digital and green technologies to advance youth led economic growth, according to the Ethiopian Embassy in India.

title: Ethiopia's Agricultural Transformation Model Offers Lessons for Other African Nations - AU Officials
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's efforts to boost agricultural productivity, promote self-sufficiency, and engage smallholder farmers offer valuable lessons for other African countries seeking to strengthen food security, according to officials from the African Union (AU) and the Regional Strategic Analysis and Knowledge Support System.

title: Sudanese Opposition Groups Reject Burhan-Backed Dialogue, Call for Alternative Peace Process
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- A group of Sudanese opposition political and civil forces has rejected a domestic dialogue initiative backed by Sovereignty Council Chairman Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.

title: Livestock Deaths and Water Scarcity Devastate Afar's Kori Woreda As El Niño Threat Grows
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A severe water and livelihood crisis is unfolding in Kori Woreda of Ethiopia's Afar Region, where residents report widespread livestock deaths, drying water sources and mounting pressure on families already struggling with prolonged drought and inadequate rainfall.

title: Egypt's Badr Abdelatty Discusses Horn Security With Djibouti Counterpart, Fourth Such Talks in a Month
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held talks with his Djiboutian counterpart Abdoulkader Houssein Omar on security and political developments in the Horn of Africa, marking his fourth such regional engagement in a month.

title: Divided By Identity, United By Demands - Fault Lines Behind Ethiopia's National Dialogue
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- On 15 July 2026, Ethiopia's long-awaited National Dialogue Conference officially commenced in Addis Abeba. The dialogue process, built around eight major thematic pillars, was concluded last week after four years marked by significant challenges and fluctuations.

title: Ethiopia's National Dialogue Lays Foundation for Nation-Building - Participants
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's National Dialogue Conference has laid the groundwork for building a resilient nation and nurturing a generation that embraces dialogue, participants told ENA.

title: Ethiopia's New Assertiveness - Dialogue, Dams and Strategic Partnerships
summary: [ENA] National Dialogue reaches a historic milestone as Ethiopia reasserts its sovereign right to develop the Abay, while diplomacy, security and strategic partnerships reinforce the country's growing regional profile.

title: Ethiopia Pushes Tourism As Strategic BRICS Cooperation Area
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has called for stronger BRICS cooperation in tourism, positioning the sector as a strategic driver of economic growth, sustainable development and people-to-people ties.

title: Ethiopia Concludes Landmark 40-Day National Dialogue
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Addis Ababa (Horndiplomat) -- Ethiopia concluded its National Dialogue Conference on Saturday after nearly 4,000 Ethiopians from diverse backgrounds spent 40 days deliberating on some of the country's most consequential national questions.

title: Sudan Says It Downed 'Hostile' Drone Launched From Ethiopian Territory
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Sudan's Defense Ministry said it shot down a "hostile" drone over Blue Nile State near the border with Ethiopia, alleging that the aircraft had been launched from Ethiopian territory.

title: Eritrean Regime Fueling Regional Conflicts, Destabilizing Neighboring Countries - Opposition Figure
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Eritrean regime is fueling regional conflicts and supporting opposition forces in neighboring countries as part of what he described as a "strategy to preserve its grip on power," Eritrean Blue Revolution Front (EBRF) Central Committee member Dawit Teferi said.

title: Ethiopia Calls for African Unity to Secure Health Sovereignty
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's Health Minister Dr. Mekdes Daba has called for stronger continental cooperation and collective action to safeguard Africa's health sovereignty and build resilient health systems.

title: WHO RC76 Participants 'Walk the Talk' in Addis Ababa, Championing Healthier Africa
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Participants of the 76th Session of the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Committee for Africa (RC76) joined a symbolic health walk on Sunday from the Adwa Victory Memorial to Meskel Square in Addis Ababa.

title: Ethiopia, U.S. Agree to Establish Comprehensive Strategic Cooperation in Defense, Security
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia and the United States have agreed to establish comprehensive strategic cooperation in defense and security.

title: Ethiopia Seeking to Unlock Banana Export Potential
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia is seeking to turn its growing banana production into a major export by improving quality, productivity and market access, according to Ministry of Agriculture.

title: Ethiopia Does Not Need Permission to Develop Abay Resources, Says Water Minister
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- "Ethiopia does not need permission from anyone to develop its water resources as it is a sovereign country," Water and Energy Minister Habtamu Itefa said.

title: UN Commends Ethiopia's Leadership for Humanitarian Action, Sustainable Solutions
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Ethiopia, Ozonnia Ojielo, has commended the Government of Ethiopia for its steadfast commitment to humanitarian action and sustainable solutions to recurring crises.

title: From Brain Drain to Brain Circulation - Rethinking Ethiopian Scholars' Role in Global Knowledge Exchange
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Each year, hundreds of young Ethiopian scholars prepare to pursue higher education at universities across Europe, North America, and Asia. Yet, as international student mobility expands, a critical philosophical question emerges: When a young Ethiopian scholar steps onto a foreign campus, must global ambition come at the expense of national loyalty, or can global citizenship strengthen state capacity?

title: Drone Strikes in Two Locations in Mekelle, 13 Casualties Received At Ayder Hospital
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba- Two drone strikes were reported in Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia's Tigray region, on Thursday, August 20, with Ayder Specialized Hospital saying it received 13 casualties from one of the strikes.

title: UAE-Linked Zijin Gold Acquires Stake in Ethiopian Gold Mine Near Sudan Border
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Chinese mining company Zijin Gold International has acquired a 9.2% stake in Canadian mining firm Allied Gold, gaining partial ownership of its portfolio that includes the Kurmuk gold project in Ethiopia's Benishangul-Gumuz Region, near the Sudanese border.

title: U.S. Judge Denies Bond for Ethiopian-Born University Instructor Held in Ice Detention
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- An immigration judge has denied a request to release Dr. Berhanu Kibret, an Ethiopian-born instructor at the University of Maryland School of Pharmacy, keeping him in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention nearly a month after he was arrested at a Texas airport.

title: Ethiopia's Forest Conservation Vital for the Horn of Africa - Norway's Envoy
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's progress in expanding forest cover and its ongoing conservation efforts are vital not only for its own people but for the wider Horn of Africa, according to Live Jacob Sydness, Norway's Climate Counsellor and Special Envoy for Climate and Forests.

title: Ethiopia's Corridor Dev't Advancing Healthier, Happier Communities - State Minister
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's expanding corridor development projects are contributing to healthier, happier and more socially connected communities by promoting walking, improving urban environments and transforming previously neglected riverbanks, State Minister of Health Frehiwot Abebe said.

title: Chinese Firms Dominate Shortlist for Ethiopia's $12.5 Billion Bishoftu Airport Project
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Chinese companies or joint ventures involving Chinese firms account for the majority of shortlisted bidders competing for the construction of Ethiopia's forthcoming USD12.5 billion Bishoftu International Airport, according to aviation intelligence provider and news portal ch-aviation.

title: Judge Allows Trump Administration to End TPS Protection for Ethiopians
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A US federal judge has ruled that the administration of President Donald Trump can terminate Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for more than 5,000 Ethiopians, clearing the way for their potential deportation despite concerns over security and humanitarian conditions in Ethiopia.

title: MSF Expands Healthcare Response in Oromia's Wollega Zones Amid Critical Service Gaps
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), also known as Doctors Without Borders, has launched a comprehensive primary and secondary healthcare support program in Ethiopia's East and West Wollega zones, seeking to restore access to essential services in areas where conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks and damaged health infrastructure have left communities with significant unmet needs.

title: Ethiopia's Birr Hits Record Low Despite Billions Spent to Support Currency
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia's birr has fallen to a record low against the US dollar despite the central bank spending about $2.2 billion this year to support the currency, Bloomberg reported, as rising import costs and strong demand for foreign currency continue to put pressure on the exchange rate.

title: U.S. Signals Readiness to Resume GERD Mediation As Nile Dispute Persists
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The United States is ready to resume mediation between Egypt and Ethiopia over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), a senior adviser to US President Donald Trump has said, signalling a renewed diplomatic effort to resolve the long-running dispute over the use and management of Nile waters.
